_note: Hand-written, not produced by the pipeline. Ten events that help explain the renewable-share chart, each with its source. Dates that come from EIA-860 are checked against plants.json by tests/test_milestones.py, so they cannot drift from the data. 'month' places the marker on the chart; 'date_text' is what the card shows.

oahu.title: Kahuku Wind starts
oahu.text: Kahuku Wind Power starts up, 30 MW of wind with a 15 MW battery, the first Oʻahu wind in EIA's data (smaller turbines ran at Kahuku from 1985 to 1996, before EIA's records begin).

oahu.title: First utility-scale solar
oahu.text: Kapolei Solar Energy Park (1 MW) becomes the first utility-scale solar farm in EIA's data, with Pearl City Peninsula (1 MW) and Kalaeloa Solar Two (5 MW) following in November and December.

oahu.title: Kawailoa Wind starts
oahu.text: Kawailoa Wind (69 MW) starts up on the North Shore and remains Oʻahu's largest wind farm.

oahu.title: Honolulu Power Plant retires
oahu.text: The Honolulu oil-fired steam plant (104 MW, two units in service since 1954 and 1957) is retired.

oahu.title: Act 97 sets a 100% renewable goal
oahu.text: Hawaiʻi's Act 97 requires 100% renewable electricity by 2045, the first such state law.

oahu.title: Net metering closes to new customers
oahu.text: The Public Utilities Commission stops taking new rooftop-solar customers into net metering (cutoff October 12), the program that credited owners at the retail rate for power sent to the grid.

oahu.title: Four solar farms come online
oahu.text: Waipio Solar (46 MW), Kawailoa Solar (49 MW), West Loch Solar One (20 MW) and Lanikuhana Solar (15 MW) start up within three months, about 130 MW in all.

oahu.title: Nā Pua Makani wind starts
oahu.text: Nā Pua Makani (27.6 MW), Oʻahu's newest wind farm, starts up at Kahuku.

oahu.title: AES coal plant closes
oahu.text: AES Hawaii's 203 MW coal plant, in service since 1992, shuts down on September 1, ending coal power in Hawaiʻi.

oahu.title: Kapolei Energy Storage starts
oahu.text: Kapolei Energy Storage (185 MW / 565 MWh), Oʻahu's largest battery, starts up.
